title: Cameras Everywhere
text:
Security cameras are now installed in many streets, shops and public buildings. Supporters say that cameras help police to find criminals and to protect people. However, some citizens feel uncomfortable because they are recorded all day long. They worry that their movements are being stored and analysed without their knowledge.

Some companies have started to use facial recognition software in their stores. The software can identify regular customers and suggest products that they might like. Although this can improve service, it also raises questions about consent. Many experts believe that clear laws are necessary to protect personal data.

questions.text: According to the passage, why do supporters say cameras are useful?
options: They help police find criminals and protect people.
They reduce the price of goods.

questions.text: What can the facial recognition software in some stores do?
options: It can identify regular customers and suggest products.
It can close the store at night.
It can speak to customers in many languages.

questions.text: Why do some citizens feel uncomfortable about being recorded?
options: They enjoy being watched by police.
They do not know how their movements are stored and analysed.
They never go out in public.
They think cameras are too cheap.

questions.text: What can be inferred about the experts' view of facial recognition in stores?
options: They think the technology has no benefits at all.
They believe clear laws should control how personal data is used.
They want all stores to stop using cameras.
They think customers should pay for the software.

paragraph_translations: Las cámaras de seguridad ya están instaladas en muchas calles, tiendas y edificios públicos. Quienes las apoyan dicen que ayudan a la policía a encontrar delincuentes y a proteger a las personas. Sin embargo, algunos ciudadanos se sienten incómodos porque son grabados todo el día. Les preocupa que sus movimientos se guarden y se analicen sin que ellos lo sepan.

Algunas empresas han empezado a usar software de reconocimiento facial en sus tiendas. El software puede identificar a los clientes habituales y sugerir productos que les podrían gustar. Aunque esto puede mejorar el servicio, también plantea dudas sobre el consentimiento. Muchos expertos creen que son necesarias leyes claras para proteger los datos personales.
